description:
Tier 2, after inflate. zstd decoding is FSE (tANS) and Huffman tables, a sequence execution loop, and a repeat-offset history; the reference decoder is plain C with SIMD only in hot copies, but the spec surface is several times inflate's (RFC 8878). Anchor: ezstd (Rustler), zstd NIFs; these run dirty for large inputs. Do it only after inflate's bit reader, table builders and growable output have proven themselves; reuse them.

Expected verdict: poor on speed vs libzstd (which is heavily tuned), with the safety and yielding argument; the honest question for the entry is whether a bounded, bounds-checked zstd decoder is worth having for untrusted archives.

Scope: frame decoding without dictionaries; window sizes up to 8 MB; dictionaries raise.

Blocked by the inflate ticket and defk-6ag.

Done when: the decoder passes the zstd test corpus for the supported subset, fuzz agreement runs, the verdict is measured and recorded even if poor.
title: zstd decode from scratch vs ezstd (follow-on to inflate)
